features.claim: Triceratops had three horns on its head.
features.quote: Its name means three horned face which it gets from having three horns on its head.

features.claim: Triceratops had a large bony frill.
features.quote: Bearing a large bony frill, three horns on the skull, and a large, four-legged body, exhibiting convergent evolution with rhinoceroses, Triceratops is one of the most recognizable of all dinosaurs and the best-known ceratopsian.

features.claim: Triceratops had a beak at the front of its jaws.
features.quote: Triceratops was a low browser with a bony beak in front of its jaws.
The jaws had close-set grinding teeth.

features.claim: Triceratops had strong limbs and short hands with three hooves and short feet with four hooves.
features.quote: Both Triceratops species possessed a very sturdy build, with strong limbs, short hands with three hooves each, and short feet with four hooves each.

features.claim: Triceratops had large, pebbled scales on its skin.
features.quote: Skin impressions have been found for Triceratops, showing that it had large, pebbled scales.

features.claim: Triceratops had a single horn on its snout above the nostrils.
features.quote: It bore a single horn on the snout, above the nostrils, and a pair of horns approximately 1 m (3 ft) long, with one above each eye.

features.claim: Triceratops had a pair of horns about one meter long above its eyes.
features.quote: The skull also featured a pair of supraorbital "brow" horns approximately 1 meter (3.3 ft) long, with one above each eye.

features.claim: Triceratops had a large skull relative to its body size.
features.quote: Like all chasmosaurines, Triceratops had a large skull relative to its body size, among the largest of all land animals.

features.claim: Triceratops was a very large animal, measuring around 8–9 m in length and weighing up to 6–10 metric tons.
features.quote: Triceratops was a very large animal, measuring around 8–9 m (26–30 ft) in length and weighing up to 6–10 metric tons (6.6–11.0 short tons).

not_this.claim: Triceratops did not have large holes in its frill like most other ceratopsids.
not_this.quote: Most other ceratopsids had large holes (fenestrae) in their frills, while those of Triceratops were noticeably solid.

not_this.claim: Triceratops did not walk with its front legs sprawling at angles from the thorax.
not_this.quote: Originally, it was believed that the front legs of the animal had to be sprawling at angles from the thorax, in order to better bear the weight of the head.

second_reading.claim: Triceratops had a vertebral column of ten neck, twelve back, ten sacral, and about forty-five tail vertebrae.
second_reading.quote: The vertebral column consisted of ten neck, twelve back, ten sacral, and about forty-five tail vertebrae.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: Triceratops was not related to rhinoceroses.
second_reading.quote: Triceratops wasn’t related to rhinoceroses at all.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: Whether Triceratops lived in herds is uncertain.
second_reading.quote: Although Triceratops is commonly portrayed as a herding animal, there is currently little evidence to suggest that they lived in herds.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: Whether Triceratops used its horns in combat with each other is disagreed upon.
second_reading.quote: While studies show that such activity would be feasible, if unlike that of present-day horned animals, there is disagreement about whether they did so.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: Whether Torosaurus represents mature Triceratops individuals is disputed.
second_reading.quote: This view has been highly disputed, with some morphometric research and the apparent existence of authentic Torosaurus subadults favoring the distinctness of the two genera, according to newer studies.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: Whether the differing Triceratops skulls represent individual variation within one or two species is uncertain.
second_reading.quote: With time, the idea that the differing skulls might be representative of individual variation within one (or two) species gained popularity.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it
